newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM gold futures slip in line with bullion.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM gold futures slip in line with bullion.

text.p: Yen-denominated Tokyo gold futures ended slightly weaker on Wednesday, as earlier bargain-hunting buying lost steam in line with dips in bullion prices and the yen's moderate rise against the dollar, traders said.
Gold prices ranged from two to eight yen per gram easier. Most-active benchmark December was off two at 1,313 yen.
Three distant months hit life-of-contract lows.

In the bullion market, spot gold edged down to $357.10/60 per ounce at 0730 GMT, against $358.50/359.00 in New York on Tuesday as some Australian producer selling pressured the market amid continued bearish sentiment.

"Despite the recent plunge in gold prices, we have not seen the floor yet. We are not expecting much buying by Japanese investors, which had been a factor to put a brake on the slide in gold," one trader said.
He saw strong support for TOCOM benchmark December at 1,304 yen, the lowest level last year, adding that spot gold may probe the downside at $355.00 within a few days.

Silver and platinum futures ended mixed, while palladium was firmer. A bullion house official said recent strength in palladium was due to good demand in Europe from auto catalyst makers amid lingering fears over Russian metal supplies.
Traders said supplies of palladium sponge, used in auto catalysts, were especially tight.
In the palladium futures market, profit-taking later in the day capped early gains.
Palladium futures ranged from flat to nine yen per gram up, with benchmark December ending up nine at 442 yen.
Benchmark December silver was down 0.7 yen per 10 grams at 175.7 yen. Benchmark December platinum was down two yen at 1,332 yen.
